misconception.text: Heat flows from a cold body to a hot one.

correction.text: Heat flows from the hotter body to the colder one, until they reach the same temperature.

correction.text: The metal conducts the heat away far faster, so it feels hotter long before the wooden one does.

explanation.text: Heating makes the fluid expand and less dense, so it rises and cooler denser fluid takes its place. That circulation carries the heat.

stem.text: The radiation emitted by a body depends on

options.text: its temperature and its surface area and colour

explanation.text: A hot dark surface radiates far better than a hot polished one, and the rate rises with the fourth power of the absolute temperature.

stem.text: The first law of thermodynamics is a statement of the conservation of

explanation.text: The first law says the change in internal energy equals the heat added less the work done by the gas.

stem.text: Heat added to a gas always raises its temperature.

explanation.text: The heat may go into raising the temperature, into doing work as the gas expands, or into both. The first law says where it goes, not where it ends.

stem.text: The efficiency of a heat engine is

options.text: the ratio of the work done to the heat absorbed
the ratio of the heat rejected to the heat absorbed
the heat absorbed divided by the work done

explanation.text: The efficiency is $\eta = W/Q_h$, the useful work as a fraction of the heat taken from the hot source. It is always less than one.
The Carnot efficiency depends only on the absolute temperatures of the source and the sink: $\eta = 1 - T_c/T_h$.

stem.text: The second law of thermodynamics says that

options.text: the entropy of an isolated system never decreases
heat flows from cold to hot spontaneously

explanation.text: The second law states that the total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease. It does not affect the conservation of energy, which is the first law.
